content:
Just after 2:45 on Monday afternoon, a tractor-trailer and a pickup truck collided at the intersection of Shiloh and Las Cruces in North Laredo. A 17-year-old boy was found without a pulse. By Monday night, he was in critical condition at Doctors Hospital.

KGNS reported that when officers arrived, Border Patrol agents were already performing CPR. Crews began life-saving treatment at the scene and rushed the teenager to the emergency department at Doctors Hospital. The intersection — plus northbound San Dario Avenue to the I-35 frontage road — was shut down for the emergency response, reopening around 8:30 p.m.

What we don't know yet

How it happened. Nothing has been reported about what caused the collision — whether a light was run, who had the right of way, or whether speed or distraction played a role. The Laredo Police Department's crash team is investigating.

Whether anyone will face charges. Nothing has been reported about the tractor-trailer driver being cited or arrested. In serious-injury crashes, that determination often comes days later, once the crash team reconstructs the scene.

The teenager's identity and condition beyond "critical." His name has not been released. Critical condition at Doctors Hospital is the last official word.

What Webb Watch is asking

Shiloh and Las Cruces is a busy North Laredo crossing — how many serious crashes has it seen this year, and has the city ever studied it for safety improvements? Will LPD release the crash team's findings publicly, and on what timeline? And what is the teenager's condition now? We are watching this one closely — a 17-year-old fighting for his life deserves answers, not just a reopened intersection.

Sources: KGNS (Angie Bravo), Oct. 19, 2026; Webb Watch 956 reporting.

— Walter Webb & Willa Webb, Investigative Reporters, Webb Watch 956

Webb Watch 956

title: A 17-Year-Old Without a Pulse: Tractor-Trailer Crash at Shiloh and Las Cruces Leaves Teen Critical
